gap: No result ChatGPT got says how quickly each kit's station switches to battery when the grid drops. Jackery says in its own words that the Explorer 1000 v2 switches in 20 ms and is 'not a 0 ms (no interruption) switching UPS', and that it should not run data servers or workstations. EcoFlow rates the DELTA 3 Classic at under 10 ms.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages: Dealectric's current page, Lights On Labs, PowerSized's kit price guide and StormWatts' same-panel-watts comparison. None of them mentions UPS or EPS mode, switchover time or pass-through. PowerSized and StormWatts cover solar input voltage and current, panel Voc and cold-morning Voc in detail, so that mechanism is already taken. Switchover time is not. I did not open EnergySage, Prepared States or SolarGenAdvisor.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. A fridge, router, lights or CPAP will run through a 10–20 ms gap on any of these kits, so the largest-battery logic still stands. It does split the kits for one common home-backup use: keeping a desktop PC, NAS or home office running unattended through an outage. There, EcoFlow's under-10 ms DELTA 3 Classic is the safer kit, and Jackery's own FAQ rules the Explorer 1000 v2 out for workstations. The page should say that for those loads the shopper should pick by switchover time, not by battery size. There is also a second fact from Jackery's own FAQ: the Explorer 1000 v2 charges only from 0 to 45 °C, so it will not take solar charge below freezing during a winter outage.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 (Explorer 1000 v2 + 200 W)

findings.label: UPS switchover time and maker's caveat
findings.note: Jackery's wording: 'automatically switches to battery power within 20 ms (0.02 seconds)'. 'This function is not a 0 ms (no interruption) switching UPS.' It also warns against connecting 'devices that require a true uninterruptible power supply, such as data servers or workstations.'

findings.label: Charging temperature range
findings.note: Below 0 °C the station will not take a charge, from solar or anything else. That matters for a winter outage if the station sits in a garage or outdoors.

findings.label: Solar input per port
findings.value: 16–60 V; one port: 10.5 A, 200 W max; both ports: 21 A, 400 W max
findings.note: The kit's single 200 W panel on one port already uses that port's full 200 W limit. Reaching the 400 W ceiling takes a second panel on the second port. Our page currently lists '400 W' with no voltage figure.
